question_text: In triangle ABC, $AB = 72\text{ cm}$, $BC = 61\text{ cm}$, and $\mathrm{A\widehat{B}C} = 43^\circ$.

mark_breakdown.desc: Cumulative frequency curve plotted correctly against upper class boundaries

subparts.solution:
Cumulative frequency table:
$7 < h \leqslant 8$: CF $= 8$
$8 < h \leqslant 9$: CF $= 8 + 59 = 67$
$9 < h \leqslant 10$: CF $= 67 + 74 = 141$
$10 < h \leqslant 11$: CF $= 141 + 22 = 163$
$11 < h \leqslant 12$: CF $= 163 + 1 = 164$
Plot points $(7, 0), (8, 8), (9, 67), (10, 141), (11, 163), (12, 164)$ and join with a smooth curve.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Cumulative frequencies are plotted against the upper boundary of each class interval.
step_by_step: Plot points at upper boundaries: $h = 8, 9, 10, 11, 12$, starting at $(7, 0)$.
Draw a smooth S-shaped curve (ogive) through the points.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Plotting points at midpoints instead of upper boundaries.

mark_breakdown.desc: Locate 50% of 164 = 82 on the cumulative frequency axis
Read correct median height from the graph

subparts.solution:
The median is the 50th percentile. As $50\%$ of $164$ is $82$, we start with the cumulative frequency $82$ and find the corresponding height.
From the graph, the median $\approx 9.1\text{ m}$.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The median corresponds to $0.5 \times N$ on the cumulative frequency axis.
step_by_step: Find 82 on the vertical axis, go across to the curve, and read down to the horizontal axis.
The corresponding height is approximately $9.1\text{ m}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Reading 50 directly from the cumulative frequency axis instead of $50\%$ of 164.
